rgb: From an overhead angle, a standing or crouching camera wearer looks down at the carpeted floor of an indoor room. About 1.2 to 2.0 metres in front of and below the wearer, a person wearing a black shirt and blue jeans lies horizontally on their side, with their head on the left and their bent legs and black-socked feet stretching rightward. They face down and slightly toward the floor area between themselves and the wearer instead of looking up at the camera. In the foreground, approximately 0.5 to 1.2 metres from the wearer and 0.3 to 0.5 metres in front of the person, a black-and-white dog rests on the carpet beside a small light-colored object near the frame's right edge. During frames 1 through 3, the dog is within arm's reach, and the wearer's outstretched hands touch and stroke its head and neck at bottom center as it faces left toward the person's head. From frames 3 to 5, the hands pull out of sight while the viewpoint rises and moves slightly backward, adding roughly 0.5 metres of distance from both the dog and the person and exposing the walls and baseboards in frame 5's upper background. While the camera withdraws in frames 4 and 5, the dog moves slightly backward toward the person's hips, partly blocking their upper legs, and turns its head to gaze straight up at the wearer, with its lower paws partially cropped by the bottom edge.
depth: A top-down view shows a carpeted indoor floor with a person curled on their left side across the upper-left and center of the frame, approximately 1.0 to 1.8 m below the standing camera wearer. A medium-sized dog lies at the lower-right, about 0.8 to 1.5 m away and 0.2 to 0.6 m in front of the person until it moves against their legs in frames 4–5. In frames 1–3, the wearer's extended hands project inward from the bottom edge at a depth of 0.3 to 0.7 m, placing the dog comfortably within arm's reach, while the person remains curled with their hands by their own head. Over frames 1–5, the wearer either steps backward or rises upright, causing both subjects to appear farther below and revealing the upper-right wall base at more than 2 m. The person's head remains at the lower-left edge, directed downward and slightly right away from the camera, whereas the dog first faces lower-left before lifting and turning its head upward to stare directly at the wearer in frames 4 and 5, partly covering the person's knees. The depth map clearly distinguishes the foreground height of the reaching forearms, the raised hip and shoulder of the person, and the dog's elevated head from the flat dark-shirt and dark-fur textures that merge in RGB. It is nevertheless unreliable where the floor gradient varies non-uniformly between frames and where the dog's head blends smoothly into the person's legs in frames 4–5.
segmentation: Throughout the five carpet-level frames, instance segmentation traces the person lying in the upper-left, 1.0 to 1.8 m from the wearer and facing downward and right away from the lens, as well as the dog positioned roughly 0.2 to 0.6 m to the lower-right and 0.8 to 1.5 m from the wearer. It also captures the wearer's left arm extending from the lower edge in frames 1–3 to touch the dog within an arm's-reach distance of 0.5–0.8 m. Between frames 1 and 5, the camera pulls back and tilts slightly upward; the wearer's arms disappear below the frame, with one of the wearer's feet appearing briefly at bottom-left in frame 3. Meanwhile, the dog changes from facing lower-left to sitting upright and looking straight at the wearer as it presses against and partly blocks the person's thighs. Despite weak RGB contrast, the masks make the crisp exterior outlines of the dark-dressed person, black-and-white dog, and reaching arm readily distinguishable from the shadowed carpet in frames 1, 2, and 5. The map's class assignments and temporal consistency are highly unreliable, however: frame 1 identifies the dog as a person; frame 2 divides the lying person into two masks and fails to segment their black shirt; frame 3 invents an enormous 'sandwich' mask across the carpet while omitting both subjects; frame 4 combines the person and dog into one 'cat' mask; and frame 5 joins them in a single 'person' mask.
pose: Against a black background, the pose visualization tries to follow skeletal keypoints in an indoor floor scene with a person lying on the left, 1.0 to 1.8 m below the camera wearer, curled on their side and facing down-right away from the camera. A dog is located 0.2 to 0.6 m to the person's lower-right and 0.8 to 1.5 m away, remaining within the wearer's arm's reach in frames 1–3. The wearer's hands extend into the lower foreground during frames 1–3, then withdraw from sight in frames 4–5 as the viewpoint recedes and the dog turns its head upward toward the camera in front of the person's legs. In the frames where detections appear, frames 2 and 5, yellow body segments show the horizontal posture and bent knees of a figure stretched across the floor, an orientation that is difficult to interpret from the dark RGB clothing alone. Nonetheless, pose estimation is severely unreliable across the sequence: frames 1, 3, and 4 entirely omit every body and the magenta hand skeletons belonging to the wearer in the foreground; frame 2 incorrectly places a human body skeleton across the dog's head and torso; and in frame 5, where the dog's head blocks the person's legs, the lying person's head and upper torso are reduced to tangled keypoints in incorrect positions.
